pk.context: 75 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Absorption is at least 50%, judged by urinary excretion of metabolites. About half of a dose is excreted in urine and 46% in feces over 5 days; most circulating metabolites are an inactive acid.
clues.substance: A bisulfate salt; the parent moiety has a molecular weight of 321.8. It is practically insoluble in water at neutral pH but freely soluble at pH 1.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 75 mg and 300 mg tablets, taken daily.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for diminished effect with two loss-of-function CYP2C19 alleles. Contraindicated with active bleeding and hypersensitivity; intracranial hemorrhage and fatal bleeding are key.
clues.indication: Acute coronary syndrome, including NSTEMI and STEMI, and recent MI, recent stroke or established peripheral arterial disease, to reduce the rate of MI and stroke.
clues.mechanism: Its CYP2C19-formed thiol metabolite irreversibly binds P2Y12 ADP receptors on platelets, blocking aggregation for the lifespan of the platelet.

tell: Its effect depends on CYP2C19 converting it to an active metabolite, and its boxed warning covers two loss-of-function alleles.
